report: Read all 21 candidate lemmas end to end. Every in-bucket difference is licensed by the ASV's own wording, not a split: הוּא suffixes take thy/thee/thine/Thy as written; מִן takes than (2), above (7), Out of (8), with (13); תַּחַת takes instead of (16) and under (5); לְ takes touching/for/at/unto/in/of as written and is unrepresented only where the ASV writes nothing for its relation (11 'reverence thou him', 16 'make princes', rule 40).

PSA.45.17 בְּכָל־דֹּר וָדֹר → 'in all generations' is rule 22's distributive repetition: כֹּל takes 'all', the first דֹּר takes 'generations', the waw and the second דֹּר are unrepresented. This is the only unrepresented waw in the chapter and it is correct.
All four BSB disagreements (11 לֽ, 16 לְ, 17 וָ, 17 דֹר) are documented convention differences under rules 40 and 22; none is an error.

Audited the seven added units the lemma table cannot see: 'thy' before suffixless יָרֵךְ (3, rule 18 closing); italic 'and' where no waw stands (4, 8); 'smell of' as a supplied lexical verb in a verbless clause (8); postposed locative 'there' (12); 'the palace' (13); 'A Psalm' where no מִזְמוֹר stands (0). No verse folds a word of the same kind into a neighbouring morpheme, so there is no hidden split.

Copula placement is consistent: prepositional predicates carry it on the preposition (5 'are in', 9 'are among', 12 'shall be with', rule 49); nominal, adjectival and participial predicates carry it (1, 6, 11, 13, 14, rule 20); the bare adverbial accusative עוֹלָם takes 'is for ever' with the supplied 'for' under rule 33.

Construct chains with מֶלֶךְ as rectum recast as English possessives are consistent under rule 29: the article takes 'the' in 5 (הַמֶּלֶךְ → 'the king's'), and the supplied 'the' goes to the possessor in 13 and 15. עַל־כֵּן → Therefore heads on עַל in 2, 7 and 17. Vocatives take their 'O' on the noun in 3, 6 and 10.

One hedged head to flag for cross-Psalter review rather than patch here: PSA.45.0 heads מְנַצֵּחַ → 'Chief Musician' on Musician, but rule 31's own tie-break (the ASV never writes 'Musician' alone for נָצַח) points at Chief. Psalm-title heads should follow the corpus precedent for לַמְנַצֵּחַ, which this briefing does not show; left unchanged so as not to create a cross-chapter split.

The four repeated notes (assimilated article → the; rectum takes of; supplied the on noun; supplied the on construct) all restate rules 12, 19, 15 and 29 and need no convention. Nothing in the chapter generalises beyond the contract; no promotions or amendments.
